prompt:
Research the official free-tier limits of the GitHub Actions service for public and private repositories (minutes, storage, concurrency). Cite the GitHub documentation page you used.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

If you're not sure about something, just say so.

response.content:
Based on the official GitHub documentation, the free-tier limits for GitHub Actions differ significantly between public and private repositories, particularly regarding billing for compute minutes. Below is a breakdown of the limits for minutes, storage, and concurrency.

### Minutes and Billing
For **public repositories**, the use of standard GitHub-hosted runners is free and unlimited. However, for **private repositories**, usage is tied to the specific GitHub plan (Free, Pro, Team, or Enterprise), with a monthly quota of free minutes. Any usage beyond this quota is billed. Notably, "Larger runners" are always charged, even in public repositories.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "The use of standard GitHub-hosted runners is free: ... In public repositories" | CLAIM: Standard runner usage is free for public repositories.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "GitHub Actions usage is free for self-hosted runners and for public repositories that use standard GitHub-hosted runners." | CLAIM: Public repositories using standard runners do not consume paid minutes.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "For private repositories, each GitHub account receives a quota of free minutes, artifact storage, and cache storage for use with GitHub-hosted runners, depending on the account's plan." | CLAIM: Private repositories have a limited quota of free minutes based on the plan.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "Larger runners are always charged for, even when used by public repositories or when you have quota available from your plan." | CLAIM: Larger runners are never free, regardless of repository visibility.

### Storage Limits
Storage limits (Artifact and Cache) apply per repository or account depending on the plan. These limits are shared with GitHub Packages for artifacts. The documentation explicitly states that GitHub Support cannot increase these storage limits.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "GitHub Support cannot increase storage limits for GitHub Actions." | CLAIM: Storage limits are fixed and cannot be increased via support.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "The artifact storage amounts shown are shared with GitHub Packages. This means your total storage across Actions artifacts and GitHub Packages storage cannot exceed the included amount for your plan." | CLAIM: Artifact storage limits are shared with GitHub Packages.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "| Plan | Artifact storage | Minutes (per month) | Cache storage (per repository) | ... | GitHub Free | 500 MB | 2,000 | 10 GB |" | CLAIM: The GitHub Free plan includes 500 MB of artifact storage and 10 GB of cache storage per repository.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "| Plan | Artifact storage | Minutes (per month) | Cache storage (per repository) | ... | GitHub Pro | 1 GB | 3,000 | 10 GB |" | CLAIM: The GitHub Pro plan includes 1 GB of artifact storage and 10 GB of cache storage per repository.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "| Plan | Artifact storage | Minutes (per month) | Cache storage (per repository) | ... | GitHub Team | 2 GB | 3,000 | 10 GB |" | CLAIM: The GitHub Team plan includes 2 GB of artifact storage and 10 GB of cache storage per repository.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "| Plan | Artifact storage | Minutes (per month) | Cache storage (per repository) | ... | GitHub Enterprise Cloud | 50 GB | 50,000 | 10 GB |" | CLAIM: The GitHub Enterprise Cloud plan includes 50 GB of artifact storage and 10 GB of cache storage per repository.

### Concurrency and Job Limits
Concurrency limits depend on the runner type and the GitHub plan. For GitHub-hosted runners, there are caps on the total number of concurrent jobs, as well as specific caps for macOS and GPU jobs. Additionally, there are limits on workflow queuing and check runs.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "| Runner type | GitHub plan | Total concurrent jobs | Maximum concurrent macOS jobs | Maximum concurrent GPU jobs | ... | Standard GitHub-hosted runner | Free | 20 | 5 | Not applicable |" | CLAIM: The Free plan allows up to 20 total concurrent jobs and 5 concurrent macOS jobs on standard runners.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "| Runner type | GitHub plan | Total concurrent jobs | Maximum concurrent macOS jobs | Maximum concurrent GPU jobs | ... | Standard GitHub-hosted runner | Pro | 40 | 5 | Not applicable |" | CLAIM: The Pro plan allows up to 40 total concurrent jobs and 5 concurrent macOS jobs on standard runners.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "| Runner type | GitHub plan | Total concurrent jobs | Maximum concurrent macOS jobs | Maximum concurrent GPU jobs | ... | Standard GitHub-hosted runner | Team | 60 | 5 | Not applicable |" | CLAIM: The Team plan allows up to 60 total concurrent jobs and 5 concurrent macOS jobs on standard runners.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "| Runner type | GitHub plan | Total concurrent jobs | Maximum concurrent macOS jobs | Maximum concurrent GPU jobs | ... | Standard GitHub-hosted runner | Enterprise | 500 | 50 | Not applicable |" | CLAIM: The Enterprise plan allows up to 500 total concurrent jobs and 50 concurrent macOS jobs on standard runners.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "The maximum concurrent macOS jobs is shared across standard GitHub-hosted runners and GitHub-hosted larger runners." | CLAIM: macOS job concurrency limits are pooled across standard and larger runners.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "Each repository is limited to events triggering a workflow run. ... 1500 events / 10 seconds / repository" | CLAIM: There is a rate limit of 1500 workflow trigger events per 10 seconds per repository.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "When the limit is reached, the workflow runs that were supposed to be triggered by the webhook events will be blocked and will not be queued. ... 500 workflow runs / 10 seconds" | CLAIM: A maximum of 500 workflow runs can be queued every 10 seconds.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "A check suite can have a maximum of 50,000 check runs." | CLAIM: A single check suite is limited to 50,000 check runs.

### Job Execution Time Limits
There are strict time limits on how long a single job can run or remain queued.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "Each job in a workflow can run for up to 6 hours of execution time. If a job reaches this limit, the job is terminated and fails." | CLAIM: Jobs on GitHub-hosted runners are limited to 6 hours of execution time.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "A job can be in the queue for 24 hours before it is automatically cancelled." | CLAIM: Jobs queued for more than 24 hours are automatically cancelled.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "Each job in a workflow can run for up to 5 days of execution time. If a job reaches this limit, the job is terminated and fails." | CLAIM: Jobs on self-hosted runners are limited to 5 days of execution time.
